# Configure cycle detection

This page describes how to deploy Agentic Analytics and connect it to Consul Agentic Runtime Fabric to contain AI agents stuck in tool-call loops. When you finish, a repeated tool call with unchanged results opens the agent's circuit, and Consul rejects that agent's later requests. To learn how detection works, refer to [Cycle detection for AI agents](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/cycle-detection).

@include '../../../global/partials/alerts/beta.mdx'

@include 'alerts/enterprise-alert.mdx'

## Workflow

Complete the following steps:

1. Prepare your applications.
1. Get the Agentic Analytics images.
1. Connect traces to the analysis queue.
1. Configure analytics and circuit enforcement.
1. Start the components.
1. Verify detection and enforcement.

## Requirements

- Consul Agentic Runtime Fabric installed, with the AI Inference Gateway and MCP Sidecar on the model and tool paths your application uses. Refer to [Install Consul Agentic Runtime Fabric](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/install).
- [Auto-instrumentation](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/observability/configure-auto-instrumentation) configured, with trace context propagation, an OpenTelemetry Collector, and a trace backend that your analytics release supports.
- A BullMQ-compatible Redis or Valkey deployment for the analysis queue.
- A protection-state store that the analytics decision path can write and the AI Inference Gateway and MCP Sidecar can read.
- Access to the IBM Container Registry (ICR) for the `csl-ag-ana`, `csl-ig-pro`, and `csl-nod-rly` images, and versions of the other Agentic Runtime Fabric components that are compatible with your analytics release.
- A behavior policy that defines agent scope, detection thresholds, circuit validity, recovery, and handling for dependency failures.

<!-- TODO: Name the supported trace backends and protection-state store types. The reference deployment uses Tempo as the trace backend. -->

## Prepare your applications

The detector can only connect a workflow's steps if your applications carry trace context and identify the agent.

1. Forward trace context on every downstream call, including delegation calls between agents. Refer to [Trace context propagation](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/observability/auto-instrumentation#trace-context-propagation).
1. Include a stable, trusted agent identity in the trace that enforcement can also resolve.

The detector needs the tool name and comparable argument and output values in the trace. Capture only representations that the analytics component supports and your data-handling policy approves. Do not turn on unrestricted capture of prompts, arguments, results, credentials, or personal data to feed the detector. Missing or redacted evidence can prevent the argument comparison or limit findings.

## Get the Agentic Analytics images

Agentic Analytics uses the `csl-ag-ana`, `csl-ig-pro`, and `csl-nod-rly` images from the IBM Container Registry. Replace `<registry>` with the registry path supplied for your distribution and `<version>` with the analytics release tag.

<Tabs>
<Tab heading="Docker">

```shell-session
$ docker pull <registry>/csl-ag-ana:<version>
$ docker pull <registry>/csl-ig-pro:latest
$ docker pull <registry>/csl-nod-rly:latest
```

</Tab>
<Tab heading="Podman">

```shell-session
$ podman pull <registry>/csl-ag-ana:<version>
$ podman pull <registry>/csl-ig-pro:latest
$ podman pull <registry>/csl-nod-rly:latest
```

</Tab>
</Tabs>

Authenticate to the registry with your container runtime's credential mechanism when required. On Kubernetes, create an image pull secret for the registry and reference it in your deployment manifests. For reproducible deployments, pin approved release tags or digests in your manifests. Do not assume that an unqualified image name resolves to the intended registry.

## Connect traces to the analysis queue

1. Confirm that you can retrieve a workflow's spans by trace ID from the trace backend.
1. Configure the trace producer to queue trace IDs as evidence arrives. The reference deployment uses a span relay. An inference-path producer must also trigger analysis for later workflow activity.
1. Set the same queue backend, queue name, and prefix on the producer and the Agentic Analytics consumer. A mismatch leaves both services running with no analysis work delivered.
1. Configure the analytics worker's trace-query endpoint and credentials.
1. Confirm that the worker can reach the trace backend from its own network, not only from your machine.

Configure the queue backend for reliable delivery:

- Set the `noeviction` memory policy on the BullMQ backend so that queue data is not evicted.
- Configure persistence and capacity for your delivery guarantees. An in-memory development queue loses pending analysis triggers when it restarts.

## Configure analytics and circuit enforcement

Configure the following inputs with the configuration schema and deployment manifest supplied with your `csl-ag-ana` release. The names describe each input. They are not literal configuration keys.

| Input | What to configure |
| --- | --- |
| Analytics image | The fully qualified `csl-ag-ana` image |
| Dependency images | The `csl-ig-pro` and `csl-nod-rly` images, or approved pinned versions, in their deployment services |
| Queue connection | Backend endpoint, authentication, queue name, and prefix shared with the producer |
| Trace source | The trace backend's query endpoint and access credentials |
| Cycle detector | Turn on cycle analysis, and set the minimum repetition count and the semantic similarity threshold |
| Analysis scheduling | Limit concurrent traces and indexing waits, and keep passes for each trace serial |
| Agent attribution | Map findings and requests to the same trusted agent identity and policy scope |
| Circuit policy | When a finding opens a circuit, the reason recorded, and the validity and recovery rules |
| Protection-state connection | Write access for the decision publisher and read access for the gateway and sidecar enforcement |
| Dependency failures | Handling for unavailable queues, missing traces, stale state, and failed state reads or writes |

Keep storage and analytics endpoints private, and grant each component only the access it needs.

## Start the components

1. Connect the analytics decision path to protection-state publication.
1. Configure enforcement in the AI Inference Gateway and MCP Sidecar to read protection state before they forward requests.
1. Start the queue and state services, the trace backend, and the collection path.
1. Deploy the analytics service with the configured image, network access, and credentials.
1. Start the trace producer.
1. Confirm that the cycle detector is turned on and consuming the expected queue.

Detection logs alone do not show that Consul can open or enforce a circuit. Verify enforcement in the next section.

## Verify detection and enforcement

Use a non-production agent workflow, and a test model or a bounded usage budget.

1. Run any workflow. Confirm that the trace producer queues its trace ID and that an Agentic Analytics worker consumes it. If no analysis runs, check this handoff first.
1. Run a workflow that calls the same tool with different arguments, such as successive `page` values, and receives new results. Confirm that the trace is analyzed and produces no finding.
1. Run a workflow that calls a tool with unchanged arguments and receives changing results. Confirm that it produces no finding.
1. Run a workflow in which one agent repeatedly calls `query_records` with `{"filter":"status:active","page":1}` and receives unchanged results. Exceed the repetition threshold. If the workflow summarizes between calls, keep the summaries unchanged too.
1. Confirm a finding for that trace and agent.
1. Confirm that behavior policy publishes an open circuit for the agent, with a reason and a validity period.
1. Send another request from the agent through the protected route. Confirm an HTTP `503` response, and confirm that the request does not reach the upstream.
1. Send a request from an unaffected agent to the same backend. Confirm that it succeeds.
1. Run the expiry or reset procedure. Confirm that Consul admits the agent's requests again.
1. Make analytics or protection-state storage unavailable. Confirm that the behavior matches your dependency-failure policy.

Check worker activity as well as queue state. An empty queue does not mean that every scheduled pass finished, and a finding does not mean that enforcement read the new state.
